title: If and When
description: Real conditions with إذا, daydreams with لو, and the future 'when' — plus the wish formulas Yemenis say a dozen times a day and the invitations that are really conditions.
approach: GPA Phase 4 — the learner hears real and unreal conditions contrasted in the same scene, then produces both about their own plans and wishes.
unlock_condition: Say one real condition with إذا, one unreal one with لو … كان, and one wish with يا ريت, all judged natural by the AI
can_do: Say what you will do if something happens
Express a wish and an unreal 'if only'

grammar.title: إذا for the possible, لو for the imaginary, متى ما for the future 'when'
grammar.explanation: إذا 'if' covers anything that might really happen. After it the verb is usually in the past even though the meaning is future — إذا جيت 'if you come' — and the result is a plain present, future or command: إذا جيت صنعاء لازم تجرّب السلتة. لو is for the unreal or the regretted: لو + past, and the result gets كان (or كنت for 'I') + past: لو كان معي زلط كان اشتريت قات حرازي 'if I'd had money I would have bought Ḥarāzi qat'. Sanaa speakers also front the result with لـ: لكان اشتريت. متى ما 'whenever / when' is the future 'when' — متى ما وصلت اتصل بي 'when you arrive, call me'. Keep إذا and لو apart: mixing them makes a plan sound like a fantasy.

examples.arabic: إذا جيت صنعاء، لازم تجرّب السلتة
examples.transliteration: idha jiit ṣanʿaa, laazim tjarrib is-salta
examples.english: If you come to Sanaa, you have to try saltah
If he doesn't come, we won't chew

examples.arabic: لو كان معي زلط كنت اشتريت سيارة
examples.transliteration: law kaan maʿi zalaṭ kunt ishtarayt sayyaara
examples.english: If I had money I would buy a car
If I had seen him I would have told him

culture.title: The invitation is a condition, and the wish is a prayer
culture.note: A Yemeni invitation is rarely a bare 'come': it is إذا فضيت 'if you're free', لو تشرّفنا 'if you'd honour us', متى ما تشتي 'whenever you like'. The condition gives you a graceful way out and the host a graceful way to insist. Wishes are prayers: يا ريت 'if only' for yourself, الله يعطيك اللي في بالك 'may God give you what is on your mind' for someone else, and إن شاء الله attached to any plan — leaving it off sounds arrogant. If someone says لو سمحت it is not a condition at all but 'please'.

phrases.english: If you're free, come and have lunch at ours
I wish, but I have work
Whenever you like, the house is yours

vocabulary.teaching_note: The 'if' of real possibilities and plans. Interdental dh. Typed اذا online. Verb after it usually in the past: إذا جيت.
vocabulary.image_scene: A signpost with two arrows, one marked with a tick, a clear sky.

example.arabic: إذا ما لقيتش تاكسي، اتصل بي
example.transliteration: idha maa ligiitsh taksi, ittaṣil bi
example.english: If you don't find a taxi, call me

vocabulary.video_hint: Plans discussed on camera; إذا opening a condition.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Imaginary or regretted conditions. Result takes كان + past. Also softens a request: لو سمحت. Not for real plans.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man daydreaming, thought bubble with a sports car and a beach.

example.arabic: لو كان معي وقت، كنت سرت عدن
example.transliteration: law kaan maʿi wagt, kunt sirt ʿadan
example.english: If I had time, I would go to Aden

vocabulary.video_hint: 'If I had a million' style talk; لو with a wistful tone.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The future 'when'. The verb after it goes in the past even for the future, just like إذا: متى ما وصلت. لما also works for future 'when' in Sanaa.
vocabulary.image_scene: A clock with no hands and a door opening onto sunlight.

example.english: Whenever you're free, let me know

vocabulary.video_hint: Arranging to meet; متى ما in the reply.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Wistful 'if only': يا ريت أقدر 'I wish I could'. Also the enthusiastic reply to an invitation you cannot accept. Typed ياريت.
vocabulary.image_scene: A young woman gazing at a plane in the sky, hand on her chin.

example.english: I wish I could travel with you

vocabulary.video_hint: Replies to invitations; يا ريت said with a sigh.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Possible / maybe / may I'. ممكن أجي بكرة 'I might come tomorrow'; ممكن أشرب ماء؟ 'may I have water?'. مش ممكن 'not possible'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A door half open with a question mark and a tick on either side.

example.english: It's possible we'll go to Hodeidah next week

vocabulary.video_hint: Plans and requests; ممكن opening a question or hedging a plan.

vocabulary.teaching_note: A tiny Yemeni word with many jobs. After a condition it means 'then, in that case': طيب عاد نسير 'OK then, let's go'. With a suffix it means 'still' (عادك هنا؟ 'are you still here?'), with negation 'anymore' (ما عاد). It can also mark the near future: عاد أسير 'I'm about to go'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man nodding decisively and pointing forward, keys in hand.

example.arabic: إذا الجو زين، عاد نطلع الجبل
example.transliteration: idha j-jaww zayn, ʿaad niṭlaʿ ij-jabal
example.english: If the weather is good, then we'll go up the mountain

vocabulary.video_hint: Any decision moment; طيب عاد before the plan.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Otherwise' after a command or condition: اسرع وإلا نتأخر. Also 'or' in questions: شاهي وإلا قهوة؟ Typed والا or ولا.
vocabulary.image_scene: A fork in a road, one branch leading to a bus, the other to a man walking.

example.english: Leave early, otherwise the bus will go

vocabulary.video_hint: Warnings and choices; وإلا between the two outcomes.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Literally 'a precaution'. خذ معك ماء احتياط 'take water just in case'. Also في حالة 'in the case that'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A backpack with a bottle of water, torch and umbrella laid out.

example.english: Take the charger with you just in case

vocabulary.video_hint: Packing and travel prep vlogs; احتياط as an item is added.

vocabulary.teaching_note: In a لو sentence, كنت + verb is 'I would': لو معي زلط كنت أشتري سيارة. The same word is 'I was' in a story — the لو tells you which. For he/she/they use كان / كانت / كانو.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man imagining himself in a new car, dotted-line outline of the car.

example.arabic: لو عندي وقت، كنت أتعلم عربي كل يوم
example.transliteration: law ʿindi wagt, kunt atʿallam ʿarabi kull yawm
example.english: If I had time, I would learn Arabic every day

vocabulary.video_hint: Hypothetical talk; كنت + verb after لو.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The 'would have' of a regret: لو جيت لكان شفته 'if you had come you'd have seen him'. The لـ marks the result; plain كان is fine too. For 'I' say لكنت.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man looking at a missed-train departure board, hand on his head.

example.arabic: لو خرجنا بدري لكان لحقنا الباص
example.transliteration: law kharajna badri la-kaan liḥigna l-baaṣ
example.english: If we'd left early we would have caught the bus

vocabulary.video_hint: Regrets narrated after a mishap; لو … لكان.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The answer to any question you cannot answer yet. على حسب الجو 'depends on the weather'; alone with a shrug it is 'it depends'. Also just حسب.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman weighing two options in her hands like a scale, a sun and a cloud above.

example.english: Are you coming tomorrow? — Depends on work

vocabulary.video_hint: Hedged answers to plans; على حسب with a shrug.

vocabulary.teaching_note: فرصة زينة 'a good opportunity'; إذا جات فرصة 'if a chance comes'. فرصة سعيدة is also the phrase for 'nice to meet you'.
vocabulary.image_scene: An open door with light streaming in and a ticket held toward it.

example.english: This is a chance that won't come again

vocabulary.video_hint: Talk about jobs and travel; فرصة as something to seize.

vocabulary.teaching_note: حظي زين 'my luck is good'; ما عندي حظ 'I have no luck'. Emphatic ẓ, doubled. بالتوفيق is what you wish someone, not حظ.
vocabulary.image_scene: A four-leaf clover on a table beside a die showing six.

example.arabic: لو كان عندي حظ كنت لقيت شغل
example.transliteration: law kaan ʿindi ḥaẓẓ kunt ligiit shughl
example.english: If I had luck I'd have found work

vocabulary.video_hint: Games and lotteries; حظ said on a win or loss.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Both a dream at night and a life dream. حلمي أسافر 'my dream is to travel'. Plural أحلام.
vocabulary.image_scene: A sleeping boy with a thought bubble showing a football stadium.

example.english: My dream is to visit Old Sanaa

vocabulary.video_hint: Personal vlogs about goals; حلمي at the start.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The classic لو subject: لو كنت غني… 'if I were rich…'. Feminine غنية, plural أغنياء.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man in a fine thawb beside a big car and a stack of riyal notes.

example.arabic: لو كنت غني، كنت بنيت بيت في الجبل
example.transliteration: law kunt ghani, kunt banayt bayt fij-jabal
example.english: If I were rich, I'd build a house in the mountains

vocabulary.video_hint: 'If I were rich' talk; غني with a laugh.

vocabulary.teaching_note: ق is g: fagiir. Also 'poor thing' in sympathy. Feminine فقيرة, plural فقراء.
vocabulary.image_scene: An old man with a small tray of goods on a street corner.

example.english: He is poor but his heart is big

vocabulary.video_hint: Charity and street vlogs; فقير in description.

vocabulary.teaching_note: سهل 'easy', سهلة for feminine. أسهل 'easier'. Learners use it about the lesson: العربي سهل؟
vocabulary.image_scene: A child solving a one-piece puzzle and grinning.

example.arabic: إذا درست كل يوم، الامتحان سهل
example.transliteration: idha darast kull yawm, il-imtiḥaan sahl
example.english: If you study every day, the exam is easy

vocabulary.video_hint: Tutorials and recipes; سهل about the task.

vocabulary.teaching_note: صعب 'hard', صعبة feminine, أصعب 'harder'. صعب شوي 'a bit hard' is the polite way to say no to a plan.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man pushing a heavy cart up a steep Sanaa lane.

example.arabic: صعب أجي بكرة، على حسب الشغل
example.transliteration: ṣaʿb aji bukra, ʿala ḥasab ish-shughl
example.english: It's hard for me to come tomorrow, depends on work

vocabulary.video_hint: Anyone describing a task or a trip; صعب with a grimace.

dialogue.speaker: Najla
dialogue.arabic: إذا فضيتي بكرة، تعالي نتغدى عندنا
dialogue.transliteration: idha fiḍiiti bukra, taʿaali nitghadda ʿindana
dialogue.english: If you're free tomorrow, come and have lunch at ours

dialogue.speaker: Sumaya
dialogue.arabic: يا ريت! بس على حسب الشغل
dialogue.transliteration: ya reet! bass ʿala ḥasab ish-shughl
dialogue.english: I'd love to! But it depends on work

dialogue.speaker: Najla
dialogue.arabic: متى ما خلصتي، اتصلي بي، عاد نجهّز الغدا
dialogue.transliteration: mata maa khallaṣti, ittaṣili bi, ʿaad njahhiz il-ghada
dialogue.english: Whenever you finish, call me, then we'll get lunch ready

dialogue.speaker: Sumaya
dialogue.arabic: لو كان الشغل أسهل، كنت جيت كل يوم
dialogue.transliteration: law kaan ish-shughl ashal, kunt jiit kull yawm
dialogue.english: If work were easier, I'd come every day

dialogue.speaker: Najla
dialogue.arabic: ممكن تجي بعد العصر، وإلا نأجّل ليوم الجمعة
dialogue.transliteration: mumkin tiji baʿd il-ʿaṣr, willa nʾajjil li-yawm ij-jumʿa
dialogue.english: You could come after the afternoon, otherwise we postpone to Friday

dialogue.speaker: Sumaya
dialogue.arabic: الجمعة أحسن، إن شاء الله. ذي فرصة ما أضيعهاش
dialogue.transliteration: ij-jumʿa aḥsan, in shaa allah. dhi furṣa maa aḍayyiʿhaash
dialogue.english: Friday is better, God willing. That's a chance I won't miss

sound_spotlight.explanation: Sanaa keeps the interdental: idha, tongue between the teeth. Egyptian iza and Gulf ida both sound foreign here.
After إذا and متى ما the verb is in the past form but the meaning is future. Hear it as a set pattern rather than translating the tense.
The لـ on كان is unstressed and runs straight into it: la-kaan. Listeners hear the result clause starting there.

lesson_sequence.detail: The Najla–Sumaya dialogue at full speed; the learner marks each line as real plan or wish.
Ten sentences, audio only, sorted into 'could happen' and 'imaginary' by the connector heard.
The 18 words with images; the result words (عاد، وإلا، كنت، لكان) grouped as the second half of a sentence.
The app gives the إذا or لو half; the learner speaks the result, choosing كنت / لكان for لو.
Picture prompts (a plane, a house, a car); the learner produces يا ريت and لو كنت غني sentences.
Role-play with the AI: invite with إذا, decline with يا ريت بس, offer an alternative with وإلا.
Counter; nudge to phrase the next real invitation as a condition.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Invite a Yemeni friend with إذا فضيت and listen for whether the answer is يا ريت or إن شاء الله — both may mean no.
real_world_prompts.context: Lesson-complete screen. Activates conditional invitations and their soft refusals.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Finish this out loud three ways: لو كان معي مليون ريال…
Ask someone تجي بكرة؟ and count how many على حسب you get in a week.
real_world_prompts.context: Recognition of hedged answers in daily life.

video_needs.scene: Street interviews or sketches on 'what would you do if you had a million'; an invitation to lunch phrased as a condition and gently declined.
